metadata.source: International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy Disease Severity Scale (ICDRDS)
metadata.citation: Wilkinson CP, Ferris FL 3rd, Klein RE, et al. Proposed international clinical diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edema disease severity scales. Ophthalmology. 2003;110(9):1677-1682.

0.name: No apparent retinopathy
0.definition: No abnormalities characteristic of diabetic retinopathy.
0.screening_guidance: Routine annual screening is typically recommended.

1.name: Mild Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (NPDR)
1.screening_guidance: Regular monitoring. Follow-up typically recommended in 6 to 12 months.

2.name: Moderate Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (NPDR)
2.definition: More than just microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR.
2.typical_findings: Microaneurysms, dot and blot hemorrhages, hard exudates, cotton wool spots.
2.screening_guidance: Closer observation required. Referral to an ophthalmologist may be considered depending on the presence of macular edema or symptom progression.

3.name: Severe Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (NPDR)
3.definition: Any of the following: >20 intraretinal hemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants, definite venous beading in 2+ quadrants, prominent IRMA in 1+ quadrant (the 4-2-1 rule), and no signs of proliferative retinopathy.
3.typical_findings: Severe hemorrhages, venous beading, intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA).
3.screening_guidance: High risk for progression to proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Prompt referral to an ophthalmologist is strongly recommended.

4.name: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR)
4.definition: One or more of the following: neovascularization, vitreous/preretinal hemorrhage.
4.typical_findings: Neovascularization of the disc (NVD), neovascularization elsewhere (NVE), preretinal or vitreous hemorrhage.
4.screening_guidance: Very high risk of severe vision loss. Immediate and urgent referral to an ophthalmologist or retina specialist is required.
